about: Damaged input files written by make_inputs.py. Feed each json-* file to every place the tool reads JSON (settings, rules, baselines, caches, lock files, manifests, hook input) and each text-* file to every line list it reads (Plugins.txt and the like). Then apply the mutations to the tool's own valid sample.

answers.read: The tool reads the file as normal and gives its normal answer.
answers.refuse: A plain refusal: the tool's refusal exit code (usually 2 or 3) and a message that names the file. A guard (a hook that allows or blocks) fails closed: it blocks.
answers.read_or_refuse: Either answer; 'preferred' says which is better when both are possible.

never: a .NET unhandled exception or stack overflow
a PowerShell error record instead of the tool's own message
an exit code of 128 or more, or a negative one
running past the case's time limit

files.why: Wrong root type: a list where the tool expects an object.
round3: StarfieldVoiceTool C5 (a soundbank JSON whose root isn't an object broke the Sound Effects list)
sf-papyrus-ref C9 (a cache of the wrong shape crashed every command)

files.why: null where the root object belongs.
round3: BuildKit C7 (a lock file holding null crashed)

files.why: 20,000 nested lists. Python's json raises RecursionError, which must become a plain refusal.
round3: papyrus-log-check C5 (a manifest nested 100,000 deep gave a RecursionError traceback)

files.why: A UTF-8 byte-order mark before an empty object (Windows PowerShell 5 and some editors write one).
round3: sf-test-plan C5 (a --pins file with a BOM was refused as not valid JSON)

files.why: UTF-16 with a byte-order mark (what Windows PowerShell 5's > writes). Read it, or refuse naming the encoding.
A 5,000-digit number. Python 3.11 and later refuse to turn more than 4,300 digits into an int (ValueError).
round3: sf-load-order C6 (a rules file with an integer over 4,300 digits gave a traceback)

files.why: A file cut short in the middle of a list (a copy that stopped, a full disk).
Bytes that are not UTF-8 inside a string. A UnicodeDecodeError traceback is the bug; a refusal or a read with replacement characters is fine.

files.must: A tool that keys a map by name ignoring case must refuse or warn naming both keys, never merge them silently.
files.why: Two keys that differ only in case.
round3: BuildKit C7 (a hand-merged lock file with case twins collapsed quietly)

files.must: The first line is SharedTest-Plain.esm; U+FEFF never becomes part of a name.
files.why: A line list (such as Plugins.txt) saved as UTF-8 with a BOM.
A line list saved as UTF-16 (Notepad's 'Unicode', PowerShell 5's >).
An empty line list is valid: nothing is listed.

mutations.how: Take one valid file the tool reads (from its own tests). For each mutation below and each key at depth 1 and 2, make one copy with that one change. Expect a normal read when the tool's docs say the key is optional, else a plain refusal that names the file. Never a traceback.

round3: sf-patch-day C4 (a baseline master entry {} gave KeyError)

list.do: replace the value with the string "12" (or "false" for a true/false value)

round3: sf-patch-day R3 (a record entry with no formid gave KeyError)
